hints: Choose k items from n without caring about order.
Because answers are modulo a prime, compute division with modular inverses.
analogy: Count ordered choices and divide by the different orders of the same chosen group.
algorithm: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to the largest n; answer fact[n]*invFact[k]*invFact[n-k] modulo 1,000,000,007.
correctness: Every k-element set has k! orderings, so dividing n!/(n-k)! by k! counts each set once.
complexity: O(M+q) preprocessing and O(1) per query; O(M) space.
